data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 purports to draw on 'published definitions from the messaging literature (e.g., Burnstein & Shapiro on exactly-once semantics)' but this cited source appears fabricated—no widely recognized publication by 'Burnstein & Shapiro' on exactly-once semantics exists in the messaging/distributed-systems literature. The problem explicitly asks the answer to be grounded in 'published definitions,' and introducing an unverifiable or invented citation undermines the answer's central evidentiary claim. Moreover, SRC_002's own third countercondition concedes that 'the terminology distinction I draw may not match published usage,' effectively admitting the answer may not align with actual published definitions—the very standard the problem demands. The framing of idempotency as purely an 'application-level' property and safety as purely a 'protocol-level' property is an idiosyncratic assertion presented as an established published distinction without genuine evidentiary support.
